value.rationale: The exact first cutoff at thirteen vertices separates global stochastically monotone reinforcement from nonmonotone odds of two almost-leafless outcomes. It informs whether a stronger likelihood-ratio comparison can be safely used for rare terminal-count inference, and reveals a finite-size phenomenon invisible to known asymptotic means and Gaussian fluctuation limits. The finite cutoff is structurally tied to the two smallest achievable leaf counts and is proven exactly, not chosen arbitrarily.
